assumptions: The exception detail screen is served live by the callback service on 127.0.0.1:8001, reachable at a list route (assumed '/exceptions') with per-exception detail at '/exceptions/<run_id>'. Exact routes were not discoverable in committed code and must be bound at execution.
Backend truth for an exception's state is workflow_runs.state in data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3, and the screen is built from ReviewPayload derived from that run.

The driver_probe workspace contains at least one NEEDS_REVIEW run and at least one terminal run; concrete run ids (shown as 1/2 in the SQL) must be bound to real rows at execution, with prior state recorded for cleanup.

Browser 'click first exception in the list' aligns with the SQL-targeted run only if the list is ordered deterministically (assumed newest-first by id); executor should bind the same run to both the URL and the SQL.

The exception detail screen is served by the 'callback' service at http://127.0.0.1:8001; the exact route (assumed /exceptions and /exceptions/{id}) is not confirmed from the checkout because the builder's new files are on a branch not present here.

The screen renders one workflow_runs row: state is workflow_runs.state, evidence derives from workflow_runs.reason plus any linked document, and owner derives from the ownership records authorization.py governs.
data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 is the live persisted store the screen reads and can be seeded with at least one exception run before the run.
The canonical state vocabulary the screen may display is bounded by GRANT_STATES / workflow_runs.state as enforced by schema.py.
unresolved_questions: What is the actual route/URL of the exception detail screen and its listing on the 127.0.0.1:8001 service? It is not present in the committed callback server, so it must be confirmed against the builder's diff before these scenarios can bind concrete paths.

AC1 requires the screen name 'who owns it', but no product requirement defines where owner is sourced (a workflow_runs column, a config default like operator_name, or an assignment table). If the backend records no owner, is the screen expected to show a default role, or to flag the obligation as unowned? This determines whether S3's 'never invent an owner' expectation is correct.

Is the exception detail screen intended to be a live per-request read of workflow_runs, or a regenerated static artifact? AC3 (and S2/S8) presume live reads; if it is a rebuilt static site, staleness is governed by regeneration timing rather than request-time reads.

AC2 says show 'the evidence the exception was raised from' — is 'raised from' the specific documents/attachments that triggered the reconciliation flag, or the full document set of the load? This changes what S4 should assert as correct vs fabricated evidence.
What is the exact HTTP route and tenant-scoping mechanism for the exception detail screen? Without it the browser/request paths in S1, S2, S5, S6 are best-effort and may need the concrete path.

Which backend column(s) carry the 'next action' and the 'owner'? The diff added 31 lines to schema.py and 88 to authorization.py, but the new columns/tables are not visible in this checkout, so S2/S3 assert on rendered text rather than a named backend field.
How is an exception's 'evidence' linked (reason text vs. a document/invoice reference vs. a raised-from source id)? S4 assumes workflow_runs.reason is the primary evidence field.

There is no acceptance criterion promising behavior when the backend is unavailable mid-view or when two operators act on the same exception concurrently; if the product intends a defined behavior there (dead_end_error / failure_recovery), it should be stated so it can be verified rather than invented here.
